title: Beni Mellal city and foothills on 4 Jul 2026
summary: On 4 Jul 2026 the radar shows Beni Mellal city and its foothills inside a 6 km circle, with built-up land on 12.2% and trees, shrub and rugged slopes on 52.5%. No flag applies to this date.

sections.heading: What the radar shows here
sections.text: The city stands out as the brightest surface, with built-up HH at 5.51 dB against a circle mean of -2.34 dB. The circle averages -13.65 dB in HV, and the HV:HH ratio over the whole circle is -11.31 dB, low because the city is so bright in HH.

sections.heading: Terrain types and what they mean
sections.text: Built-up land has an HV:HH ratio of -16.14 dB, the double-bounce signature of walls. Trees, shrub and rugged slopes, 59.32 km2, give the strongest HV of the land types around the city, -12.81 dB, from volume scattering in leaves and branches. Rough dry ground and fields, 30.89 km2, sit at -18.61 dB in HV. Changing fields cover 5.4 km2 at -15.92 dB in HV.

sections.heading: Data quality notes
sections.text: No flag applies. One track only, so slopes facing away from the radar can fall in shadow. Possible cause of the strong HV on the type with trees: orchards and shrub around the city as well as the hill slopes; the optical photo would show which.
